pr.title: Remove the clean label when a push gives a pull request a new head
pr.head: 2740bd795bdc0c19a653a7fb0df63a5a215c7c03

summary: Projector's reviews label a pull request clean when the newest review of its current head found nothing to fix. A push gives the pull request a new head that no review has read, so the label has to come off. In a repository that requires the projector/review status, project init writes a GitHub Actions workflow that removes the label on each push. This repository requires that status on main, but it did not have the workflow, so a pull request kept a clean label from the review of an older head.

This change commits the two files project init writes here, unchanged: the workflow, and a .projector.toml that records the answer to the question init asks about the required check. The workflow runs from main, so it takes effect only after this pull request merges.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• clean: the label a review adds when it signs the current head off.
  • projector/review: the commit status a review posts, success when it signs the head off. The Projector review ruleset requires it on main.
  • pull_request_target: a workflow trigger that runs the default branch's copy of the workflow with a token that can edit the pull request, even one from a fork.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: One Projector review at 2740bd7, clean, with no finding threads. It suggested correcting one sentence of the pull request body, which says the .projector.toml setting makes reviews post projector/review. The ruleset on main is what makes them post it.

groups.title: The workflow that removes a stale clean label
groups.kicker: A push to a pull request that carries clean takes the label off, unless the new head is already signed off.
intro: The workflow runs on each push to a pull request, and its job starts only when the pull request carried clean at the push. Its one step reads the pull request as it is when the step runs, because a job can run late or be re-run from an old event.

1. It keeps the label on a signed-off head. When the current head already has a success projector/review status, a review signed it off after the push, so the step leaves the label.
  2. Otherwise it removes the label. It then reads the status again, and gives the label back when a review signed the head off while the step ran.
  3. It takes the label off again after a race. When a push moved the head while the step gave the label back, it removes the label once more.

files.note: The workflow exactly as project review workflow prints it in Projector 0.8.17.

checks.text: The file is byte-identical to project review workflow at this head and in the installed 0.8.17, checked with diff. So project init reports it unchanged, and a later release that changes the workflow replaces it.

The job checks out no pull request code. It passes gh only the pull request number, the repository, and the label's own spelling, each quoted, so the write token never runs code a pull request supplies.

This status read is what keeps a late job from taking clean off a head a review already signed off. It works only because the Projector review ruleset requires projector/review on main, so every review posts it.

groups.title: The recorded answer to init's question
groups.kicker: A repository setting that tells later init runs to keep the ruleset and the workflow without asking.
intro: project init asks whether the repository relies on Projector alone to sign off pull requests. review.require_check = true records a yes, so a later init asks nothing and recreates whichever of the ruleset and the workflow is missing.

files.note: Records review.require_check = true, in the exact form init writes.

checks.text: write_value at this head writes these two lines byte for byte, and project config get review.require_check reads true in the worktree.
publish never reads this key. It posts projector/review wherever the default branch's rules require it, so the setting does not by itself make reviews post the status the workflow reads.
